audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL consensus mechanisms (difficulty bomb delay EIP-4345, Clique PoA EIP-225), EVM bytecode validation (EIP-3541 0xEF rejection), historical data pruning (EIP-4444), wallet RPC chain switching (EIP-2015), fork identification networking (EIP-2124), Cancun fork module structure, KZG cryptographic primitives, Prometheus metrics (EIP-2159), and SSZ progressive containers (EIP-7495). Both EL and CL are materially present.

misclassified_entities.reason: Local signer is an internal component of the Clique node, not an external entity. It is the node's own signing key, under direct control of the system.
Blob verification caller is an internal system component (block validation pipeline) requesting KZG proof checks, not an external entity.
Blob Transaction is a data structure within the system, not an external entity. The actual external entity is the user/submitter of the transaction.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes communicate over unauthenticated P2P network. Any node can send blocks, transactions, or data requests. Covers EXT-PEER-NODE, EXT-REQUESTING-PEER, EXT-REMOTE-PEER from source files.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer / Miner via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners/block producers submit blocks that must meet difficulty targets. Blocks arrive over unauthenticated P2P, requiring full validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Authorized Signer via Clique P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Clique block headers with embedded votes (beneficiary + nonce)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Although signers are authenticated via ECDSA signature recovery, any signer can be compromised. Vote data in block headers must be validated against signing limits and majority thresholds. Default UNTRUSTED because authentication alone does not guarantee honest behavior.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can submit contract deployment transactions via public JSON-RPC. Init code and resulting bytecode are fully untrusted and must pass 0xEF first-byte validation (EIP-3541).

trusted_external_entities.name: Node Operator via Configuration
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Node operators provide bootstrap checkpoints. Authenticated via local configuration access (requires system-level trust), but checkpoint content must still be validated against known state roots. Semi-trusted because compromise enables long-range attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: External Data Provider via Out-of-Band Channels
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: IPFS, Portal Network, The Graph, torrent (historical data retrieval)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Out-of-band historical data sources (EIP-4444) are fully untrusted. Data integrity must be verified against known state roots or accumulator proofs. Any provider could serve falsified data.

trusted_external_entities.name: dApp via Wallet RPC (wallet_updateEthereumChain)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: dApps request chain switching via wallet RPC. Any web application can invoke this method. Requests may contain malicious RPC URLs (SSRF) or phishing chain parameters. Covers EXT-DAPP and EXT-MALICIOUS-DAPP.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote RPC Endpoint via HTTPS
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC endpoints provided by dApps in chain switch requests are fully untrusted. May point to internal resources (SSRF), respond with mismatched chainIds (phishing), or be MitM-attacked.

trusted_external_entities.name: Discovery Network via discv4/discv5
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: ENR exchange in peer discovery (fork ID advertisement)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Discovery network is unauthenticated. Peers can lie about fork IDs in ENRs. No cryptographic proof of fork ID correctness exists. Used for pre-filtering but cannot be solely relied upon.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted Byte Input via Transaction/Block Data
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: KZG commitment/proof bytes in blob transactions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Raw byte inputs for KZG operations originate from untrusted blob transactions. G1 points and BLS field elements must be validated (infinity check, modulus check, BLS verification) before use in cryptographic operations.

trusted_external_entities.name: Prometheus Server via HTTP Scrape
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Metrics endpoint is accessible via HTTP. Without authentication, any party can scrape operational metrics (sync state, peer count, block height), potentially leaking operational intelligence. Default UNTRUSTED as the spec does not mandate authentication.

trusted_external_entities.name: SSZ Serialized Data Source via P2P/Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Serialized SSZ containers from network sources are untrusted. Deserialization must validate active_fields bitvector, field counts, and container schema constraints. Malformed containers could exploit deserialization logic.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client / Smart Contract Verifier via Merkle Proofs
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Merkle proof submission for container field verification
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light clients submit Merkle proofs for verification. Proofs are untrusted and must be verified against expected gindices and active_fields mix-in to prevent forgery.

trusted_external_entities.name: dApp via JSON-RPC (historical data requests)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: dApps requesting historical data older than retention window are untrusted callers. Requests may attempt to trigger resource-intensive lookups or out-of-band fetches.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All blocks must pass full validation: difficulty check (EIP-4345 fake block number), Clique signer authorization (EIP-225), signing limit enforcement, timestamp validation, and extraData format verification.

Requests for historical data must be evaluated against HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS retention window (EIP-4444). Data older than threshold SHOULD NOT be served. Request rate limiting required to prevent resource exhaustion.
Block difficulty must match expected value calculated using fake block number (max(0, block.number - 10,700,000) post-Arrow Glacier). Mismatch results in block rejection.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Clique block header (beneficiary + nonce vote fields)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Signer must be recovered from ECDSA signature and verified against authorized set. Signing limit (1 per floor(N/2)+1 blocks) must be enforced. Votes require majority threshold (>50%) for execution. Epoch vote reset prevents unbounded vote accumulation.

After init code execution, returned runtime bytecode must be checked for 0xEF first byte (EIP-3541). If code[0] == 0xEF, exceptional abort consuming all gas. Applies to direct deployment, CREATE, and CREATE2 opcodes.
Checkpoint must be validated as within acceptable time bounds. Invalid checkpoint must be rejected. HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS must exceed weak subjectivity period to ensure checkpoint data availability.

All externally-sourced historical data must be verified against known state roots or accumulator proofs. Data failing integrity checks must be rejected. No implicit trust in any external data provider.

RPC URLs must be sanitized (URL format, protocol, private IP blocking). ChainId must be validated against known chain list. User confirmation required before switching. SSRF and phishing detection controls must be enforced.
RPC endpoint responses must match requested chainId. HTTPS required. Internal/private IP ranges must be blocked to prevent SSRF. Response timeouts must be enforced.

Fork IDs in ENRs are not cryptographically proven. Used only for pre-filtering, not security decisions. Full fork compatibility must be validated during ETH handshake. CRC32 collision risk accepted as low but non-zero.

48-byte inputs must pass G1 point validation (infinity check + BLS verification). 32-byte inputs must be less than BLS modulus. Pairing check must verify proof correctness. Trusted setup integrity assumed.

Metrics endpoint should be access-controlled (bind to localhost or require authentication). Exposed metrics (sync state, peer count, block height) constitute operational intelligence that could aid attack timing.

Deserialization must validate: container non-empty, max 256 fields, no trailing zeros in active_fields, field count matches active_fields popcount. Absent fields default to zero. active_fields mix-in prevents hash collision between absent and zero-valued fields.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Merkle proof verification with stable gindices
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Proofs must be verified against expected gindex positions and root hash. active_fields mix-in must be checked to prevent collision attacks. Proof path must be complete from leaf to root.
Requests for data beyond retention window should return appropriate errors or trigger out-of-band retrieval with full validation. Must not cause unbounded resource consumption.
